liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Werewolves of London** (6 reviews): Werewolves had been played in a few late-1970s shows, then shelved before this Halloween performance; Opening Werewolves of London was a novelty, though the reviewer called the show their worst of 60+ [21][23][24][25][28][30]
- **Looks Like Rain** (2 reviews): Bobby's screaming in Looks Like Rain is singled out as a highlight, likened to Estimated Prophet; Looks Like Rain is remembered as one of the best the reviewer ever saw [22][27]
- **Spooky Space** (1 review): The opening Space is described as eerie, comical and disturbing [24]
- **Shakedown Street** (1 review): Shakedown Street is pretty good, while Ship of Fools disappoints [25]
- **Ship of Fools** (1 review): The jam in Ship of Fools was prime, and Shakedown Street was great [26]
- **Space** (1 review): Space was ethereal; a companion kept calling it beautiful [29]
- **Dear Mr. Fantasy** (1 review): Dear Mr. Fantasy emerging from the second space is called cool [24]
- **Funiculi Funicula** (1 review): The show opened with a wild, spacey Funiculi Funicula [22]

## Setlist highlights

- **Crowd/Tuning 'Funiculi Funicula'**: back after 246 archived shows (1302 days); mythic rare: 2 archived performances [33]
- **Spooky Space**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [33]
- **Werewolves of London**: back after 413 archived shows (1971 days); rare: 12 archived performances [33]
- **NFA - Crowd**: earliest performance in the archive; rare: 3 archived performances [33]

## The recordings

- **gd85-10-31.matrix.loy.31189.sbeok.flacf** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 20 songs; 137 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [1]
- **gd1985-10-31.168185.senn.me80.hessberg.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 21 songs; 131 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [3]
- **gd1985-10-31.164118.akg451.ck8.eaton.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 20 songs; 129 min [5]
- **gd1985-10-31.mtx.loy.30829.sbeok.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 18 songs; 137 min [8]
- **gd85-10-31.aud-fob.sacks.2249.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 18 songs; 138 min; rated 4.14/5 by 7 [9]
- **gd85-10-31.sbd.19209.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 17 songs; 120 min; rated 2.83/5 by 6 [20]. Said about its sound: Rated B+: thick, full sound, not crisp, somewhat bassy, with light background hiss; a decent board [30]

## Around the show

- This was the only South Carolina show the Dead ever played; a row of jack-o-lanterns lined the stage front [21]
- The band began with a very long tuning session after the lights went down [21]
- Reviewer walked to the show from home through the tunnel below Assembly Blvd; it was their first show [22]
- Jack-o-lantern set design, outlandish costumes, and heavy rain; Looks Like Rain suited the weather, and Hurricane Gloria followed the tour [26]
- Costumed freaks on Halloween were a spectacle; reviewer came from Charlotte as a high school junior [27]
- Reviewer drove from Wofford College in Spartanburg; leaving, the clouds looked impossibly low and fast-moving [29]
- The show opened with Spooky Space leading into Werewolves of London [1]
- The Columbia show was the Dead's only South Carolina show [35]
- Reviewer recommends the second Fox night or one of the Richmond shows over this one [23]
- After Music Never Stopped the first set sags, and the reviewer thinks the band cut the second set short after drums [25]
- Judged better than the preceding Fox shows but perhaps not up to the following Richmond shows [26]
- First set is great, but the show loses intensity in the second set [28]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd85-10-31.matrix.loy.31189.sbeok.flacf**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: Soundboard patched with Audience [1]
- **gd1985-10-31.168185.senn.me80.hessberg.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Michael Hessberg; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Michael Hessberg's Master Audience Cassettes; Sennheiser ME-80 mics > Sony D5M [3]
- **gd1985-10-31.164118.akg451.ck8.eaton.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Rob Eaton; transferred by Rob Eaton, Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Rob Eaton's Master Audience Cassettes; AKG 451's w/ CK8 shotguns > Sony D5M [5]. Also: Recorded by Rob Eaton with AKG 451 mics; Oade Schoeps source patches Tennessee Jed, Drums and Space [5]
- **gd1985-10-31.mtx.loy.30829.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Loy; source: Matrix mix (SBD/AUD) [8]. Also: Oade source: Schoeps CMC441 through Oade M118 and modified Sony PCM-F1; Doug Oade applied DSP, and it was the lowest generation [8]
- **gd85-10-31.aud-fob.sacks.2249.sbeok.shnf**: source: FOB PCM AUD -- ??? Mics -> PCM -> DATs -> CDR (x1) -> EAC -> SHN [9]. Also: Reviewer's old analog copy of set one was a fifth-generation audience tape with plenty of hiss [28]
- **gd85-10-31.sbd.19209.sbeok.shnf**: source: S:D>C>D>C>D>CDR [Note: See info file for further details]Lineage: Cassette > D8 > Sony R500>HHB CDR800Toast 1.1 for Wav via an archive.org user [20]

## Art and photos

- Poster by LiveGRATEFUL.net: [Grateful Dead 1985-10-31 Thu Halloween Carolina Coliseum Arena, Univ. of S. Carolina, Columbia, SC](https://www.livegrateful.net/post/1319443064475/grateful-dead-1985-10-31-thu-halloween) [39]
- Fan art by Joe Jackson: [Halloween 1985: The Only Time the Grateful Dead Played in South Carolina – Extra Chill](https://extrachill.com/halloween-1985-the-only-time-the-grateful-dead-played-in-south-carolina/) [40]
- Poster by Jerry Garcia: [1985-10-31 Ticket - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/image/1985-10-31-ticket/) [41]

claims.text: This was the only South Carolina show the Dead ever played; a row of jack-o-lanterns lined the stage front
Werewolves had been played in a few late-1970s shows, then shelved before this Halloween performance
The band began with a very long tuning session after the lights went down
Reviewer walked to the show from home through the tunnel below Assembly Blvd; it was their first show
The show opened with a wild, spacey Funiculi Funicula
Bobby's screaming in Looks Like Rain is singled out as a highlight, likened to Estimated Prophet
Opening Werewolves of London was a novelty, though the reviewer called the show their worst of 60+
Reviewer recommends the second Fox night or one of the Richmond shows over this one
The opening Space is described as eerie, comical and disturbing
Werewolves was sloppy, with forgotten words and verses
Dear Mr. Fantasy emerging from the second space is called cool
A short jam leads into Werewolves, complete with howling; the opener is called extraordinary
Shakedown Street is pretty good, while Ship of Fools disappoints
After Music Never Stopped the first set sags, and the reviewer thinks the band cut the second set short after drums
Jack-o-lantern set design, outlandish costumes, and heavy rain; Looks Like Rain suited the weather, and Hurricane Gloria followed the tour
The jam in Ship of Fools was prime, and Shakedown Street was great
Judged better than the preceding Fox shows but perhaps not up to the following Richmond shows
Looks Like Rain is remembered as one of the best the reviewer ever saw
Costumed freaks on Halloween were a spectacle; reviewer came from Charlotte as a high school junior
Called the best Werewolves the Dead ever performed; the opening runs space, Funiculi Funicula, space, then Werewolves
Reviewer's old analog copy of set one was a fifth-generation audience tape with plenty of hiss
First set is great, but the show loses intensity in the second set
Space was ethereal; a companion kept calling it beautiful
Reviewer drove from Wofford College in Spartanburg; leaving, the clouds looked impossibly low and fast-moving
Rated B+: thick, full sound, not crisp, somewhat bassy, with light background hiss; a decent board
Werewolves is fun, with great MIDI effects from Jerry
The show opened with Spooky Space leading into Werewolves of London
Master cassette recorded by Michael Hessberg, transferred by Charlie Miller; Oade Schoeps source supplies an 18-second patch in Drums
Recorded by Rob Eaton with AKG 451 mics; Oade Schoeps source patches Tennessee Jed, Drums and Space
Oade source: Schoeps CMC441 through Oade M118 and modified Sony PCM-F1; Doug Oade applied DSP, and it was the lowest generation
The Columbia show was the Dead's only South Carolina show
